newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Izetbegovic aims to reintegrate Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Izetbegovic aims to reintegrate Bosnia.

text.p: Moslem leader Alija Izetbegovic, in his first statement since winning election as head of Bosnia's new three-man presidency, said on Wednesday his goal was to reintegrate the country.
He also said voting irregularities in Bosnian Serb territory had flawed the poll.
Izetbegovic, 70, narrowly beat his Serb nationalist rival Momcilo Krajisnik to head the collective presidency which will also include Croat Kresimir Zubak.

In a statement broadcast on Sarajevo-based Moslem Radio Hajat, Izetbegovic said: "I would like to thank the citizens who showed their confidence in me, being fully aware of the responsibility which I am assuming with this office."
He added: "In my comment on the results, I would just like to reiterate my political goal -- in brief, it is the reintegration of the country and justice."
But in a news conference, Izetbegovic said major irregularities had taken place in Bosnian Serb territory during the weekend elections.
"The results confirm my doubts about irregularity of the election in the Serb entity," he told reporters.
Izetbegovic said voter registration lists should be rechecked in the Serb Republic.
"Clear and major irregularities exist," he said, adding that polls should be rerun in areas where they were found.

Izetbegovic said his Party for Democratic Action (SDA) had submitted complaints to the international organisers of the poll, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), and others were still being prepared.
Izetbegovic polled 729,034 votes to Krajisnik's 690,373 and Zubak's 342,077.
Robert Frowick, head of the OSCE mission in Bosnia, said the turnout in the semi-autonomous Serb Republic was very high.

He said there were 1,010,000 eligible voters in Serb territory and that 1,023,000 cast ballots. Frowick explained the apparent discrepancy by saying Moslem refugees living abroad had cast absentee ballots but he had no specific figures.
Some 13,000 to 20,000 displaced Moslems also crossed into Serb territory to vote on election day.
